run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-17T05:40:22Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate warning for otel-demo/frontend-proxy is explained by a short, checkout-path-only error burst that coincides with a restart of the otel-demo/payment Deployment. Deployment payment rolled at 05:40:39-05:40:42Z (new ReplicaSet payment-7b6bfb9fb4, pod payment-7b6bfb9fb4-fwlht Scheduled/Pulled/Created/Started; old pod payment-55766d76b9-cpgm4 Killing), with an unchanged pod template that only carries kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-17T05:40:39Z. The payment container declares containerPort 8080 with readinessProbe, livenessProbe and startupProbe all null, and the Deployment runs a single replica, so replacing its only pod removed the sole backend for PaymentService/Charge with nothing readiness-gating traffic. All errors in this episode sit on the checkout path: service checkout's oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge and oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder spans, service frontend's POST/POST /api/checkout/executing api route (pages) /api/checkout/grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder spans, and frontend-proxy's ingress and 'router frontend egress' spans, with frontend-proxy access logs showing POST /api/checkout -> 500 'via_upstream' (upstream 'frontend') from 05:40:58.954Z to 05:42:25.071Z, and proxy error spans back at their ~05:20-05:38 background level by the windows ending ~05:48-05:56. Payment's own spans carry zero status_code ERROR and every charge it received in 05:47:32-05:47:58 logged 'Charge request received.' followed by 'Transaction complete.', so the failures were transport-level during the pod swap rather than application declines; the flagd setting paymentFailure=100% is reported as an unproven hypothesis because the ConfigMap is post-window state and is contradicted by those completed charges. The alert rule/value itself and the identity of whoever issued the restart could not be verified (see gaps).

claims.text: frontend-proxy's error-status span count jumped during the incident: 5m increases over STATUS_CODE_ERROR were 1.09 in the window ending 05:41, 87.78 ending 05:42 and 133.3-134.4 across 05:42-05:44, then fell back to 2.2-3.3 in the windows ending 05:48-05:56.

frontend-proxy carried errors on both of its operations: 20m error-status increases of 69.12 for span_name 'ingress' and 62.74 for span_name 'router frontend egress' at the last evaluated point, so its inbound spans and its egress call to frontend failed together.

There was a much smaller error baseline before the episode: frontend-proxy's 20m error-status increases were 1.25 at ~05:20 rising to ~11.3 by ~05:38, and services ad, fraud-detection and recommendation each held only about 1-2 error spans per 20m, two orders of magnitude below the 127-134 reached after 05:42.
Service frontend reported 0 error-status spans in every 5m window up to 05:41, then 164.44 (window ending 05:42) and 262.22, and 0 again from the window ending 05:48 onward.

Every frontend error span in 05:25-06:01 was on the checkout path: 'POST', 'POST /api/checkout', 'executing api route (pages) /api/checkout' and 'grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' each carried ~60.5-62.4 error spans per 20m, while 'GET /api/cart', 'POST /api/cart', 'GET /api/data', 'executing api route (pages) /api/data', 'grpc.oteldemo.CartService/GetCart', 'grpc.oteldemo.CartService/AddItem', 'grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds' and 'tcp.connect' stayed at 0.

In service checkout the only spans with error status were 'oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge' and 'oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' (24.64 error spans each against 651.28 unset per 20m), while 'oteldemo.CartService/GetCart', 'oteldemo.CartService/EmptyCart', 'oteldemo.CurrencyService/Convert', 'oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct', 'orders publish', 'HTTP POST' and 'prepareOrderItemsAndShippingQuoteFromCart' reported no error status.

frontend-proxy's access log shows POST /api/checkout answered 500 'via_upstream' with upstream 'frontend' (for example at 05:42:06.919Z, 05:42:07.709Z and 05:42:24.261Z); 8 such 500 lines fall in the 05:30-05:41 window (newest 05:40:58.954Z) and 51 in the 05:41-05:44 window (newest 05:42:25.071Z), while only two non-checkout 5xx lines appeared in 05:40-05:44 (503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started on GET /api/products at 05:42:13.801Z and 05:43:12.390Z).

Deployment payment applied a rollout at 05:40:39-05:40:42Z: 'Scaled up replica set payment-7b6bfb9fb4 from 0 to 1' with pod payment-7b6bfb9fb4-fwlht Scheduled, Pulled, Created and Started, followed by 'Scaled down replica set payment-55766d76b9 from 1 to 0', ReplicaSet payment-55766d76b9 SuccessfulDelete and Pod payment-55766d76b9-cpgm4 Killing with message 'Stopping container payment' at 05:40:42Z.

The payment pod template is unchanged apart from the restart marker: ReplicaSets payment-55766d76b9 (0 replicas) and payment-7b6bfb9fb4 (1 replica) both use image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-payment with identical env (PAYMENT_PORT 8080, FLAGD_HOST flagd, FLAGD_PORT 8013, OTEL_* settings) and identical requests/limits, and only the new template carries metadata annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-17T05:40:39Z; Deployment payment is at generation 2, revision 2, with RollingUpdate maxSurge/maxUnavailable 25%.

payment runs a single replica (Deployment payment REPLICAS/READY/AVAILABLE = 1/1/1), the only payment pod is payment-7b6bfb9fb4-fwlht started 2026-11-17T05:40:39Z and owned by ReplicaSet payment-7b6bfb9fb4, and its container declares only containerPort 8080 with readinessProbe, livenessProbe and startupProbe all null.

The payment Deployment's pod replacement at 05:40:39Z aligns with the failing path: every error in this episode is on the PaymentService/Charge call reached through checkout, the first frontend-proxy POST /api/checkout 500 follows the old pod's Kill by ~16 s at 05:40:58.954Z, and the last one is at 05:42:25.071Z while the replacement payment container was still starting.

Payment's own telemetry shows no application-level failure: service payment reported STATUS_CODE_ERROR 0 at every 5m point from 05:40 to 05:56 (and 0 over 20m), and its log holds 207 'Transaction complete.' lines in 05:38-05:48 (newest 05:47:58.693Z), with samples showing 'Charge request received.' immediately followed by 'Transaction complete.' at 05:47:32-05:47:58; none of its 605 retained lines matched error, fail, panic, exception, declin, invalid or unavailable.

No pod damage accompanied the change: all 21 otel-demo Deployments report 1/1/1 replicas and all 21 pods are Running with restartCount 0 and lastState/exit code '<none>' (no OOMKilled, Evicted or BackOff), so the payment disturbance was a controller rollout rather than a crash or eviction.

A fault-injection flag may also be involved: ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config sets the flag 'paymentFailure' (description 'Fail payment service charge requests n%') to defaultVariant '100%', with the other fault flags (adFailure, adHighCpu, adManualGc, cartFailure, emailMemoryLeak, imageSlowLoad, kafkaQueueProblems, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure) all at 'off'. It matches the failing operation by name, but it is not established as this episode's trigger: the ConfigMap reflects state at 06:02Z, after the window, and a 100% charge-failure setting contradicts the 207 charges that completed while it reads 100%.

Add a readinessProbe to the payment container, set an explicit terminationGracePeriod, and run more than one replica (or a PodDisruptionBudget) so that replacing payment's only pod cannot remove the last serving Charge backend; then re-test a rolling restart to confirm POST /api/checkout no longer returns 5xx.

gaps: Change history is not an integrated source in this Run, so who or what applied the payment rollout (annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-17T05:40:39Z) is unknown; the restart is a mechanism whose trigger could not be read.

The alerting rule 'RequestErrorRate' was not found in this Prometheus (query by rule_name and by type=alert both returned nothing), so the rule expression, threshold, evaluation window and the reported current value 0.01111111111111111 could not be verified, and the alert's startsAt 05:40:22Z precedes the first observed 500 at 05:40:58.954Z.

Jaeger holds no traces for the incident minutes: frontend-proxy trace searches returned no spans for 05:40-06:01 (one earlier query hit RESULT_TOO_LARGE with source_end_at 05:28:47), and the stored sample read back from 05:28:45-05:28:47 contains only HTTP 200 spans, so span-level error details and the gRPC status of the failing Charge call during the episode are unknown.

kube-state-metrics series are absent from this Prometheus (kube_deployment_status_replicas_ready/_available and all kube_* name queries returned nothing), so payment's ready-replica count during the rollout could not be charted.
The flagd pod's streams (init-config, flagd, flagd-ui) returned 0 bytes for 05:20-05:55, so no flag evaluation or flag-change event was observed; flagd-config content is post-window state only.

payment's retained container log begins around 05:41:30 (605 lines, 302 of them matches), so charge behaviour between the pod swap at 05:40:42 and ~05:41:30 is not observable in logs; that query was also limited to the newest 60 of 302 matching lines.

The proxy access-log scans for 05:44-05:47 and 05:47-05:50 returned no matching 500 lines but several access-log queries hit the 4 MiB read limit or a line limit, so the exact end of the 500 burst is bounded only by metric series returning to background around 05:47-05:48.

The checkout container's log windows inspected showed only successful 'payment went through' / 'order placed' lines (25 of 1902 matching, newest 05:49:59), and checkout's own error lines during 05:40-05:42 were not captured, so the checkout-side message for the failed charges is unknown.
next_steps: Review audit or change records for the payment Deployment rollout at 2026-11-17T05:40:39Z to identify the actor and whether a flag change was intended alongside it.
Confirm whether the flagd paymentFailure variant '100%' is intentional, and if it was toggled during the window, correlate it with flag-change history (not available in this Run).
Add a payment readiness probe plus a second replica or PodDisruptionBudget and re-test a rolling restart to confirm the checkout path no longer returns 5xx.
